content: 1. Acute nasopharyngitis, commonly referred to as the common cold, is an acute infection of the upper respiratory tract. 2. Acute sinusitis is an inflammation of the sinuses, often caused by infection. 3. Acute pharyngitis refers to inflammation of the pharynx, which can be caused by various pathogens, including Streptococcus bacteria (strep throat). 4. Streptococcal pharyngitis, or strep throat, is a bacterial infection of the throat caused by group A Streptococcus. 5. Acute pharyngitis can also be caused by other specified organisms or remain unspecified when the causative agent is not identified. 6. Acute tonsillitis is an infection and inflammation of the tonsils, often caused by viral or bacterial pathogens. 7. Acute laryngitis is the inflammation of the larynx, often resulting in hoarseness or loss of voice. 8. Acute tracheitis is an infection of the trachea, typically bacterial in origin. 9. Acute laryngotracheitis involves simultaneous inflammation of the larynx and trachea. 10. Acute obstructive laryngitis, commonly known as croup, is characterized by a barking cough and stridor due to airway obstruction. 11. Acute epiglottitis is a life-threatening condition involving inflammation of the epiglottis, which can obstruct the airway. 12. Acute upper respiratory infections can involve multiple or unspecified sites within the upper respiratory tract. 13. Influenza caused by an identified avian influenza virus is a specific type of flu originating from avian species. 14. Influenza caused by an identified influenza virus can present with pneumonia, other respiratory symptoms, or systemic manifestations. 15. Influenza with pneumonia occurs when the influenza virus directly causes lung infection. 16. Influenza with other respiratory manifestations includes symptoms such as bronchitis or sinusitis caused by the influenza virus. 17. Influenza with other systemic manifestations may involve symptoms like myositis or encephalopathy. 18. Influenza with an unidentified virus can also present with pneumonia, respiratory symptoms, or systemic manifestations. 19. Viral pneumonia, not elsewhere classified, includes pneumonia caused by viruses such as adenovirus. 20. Adenoviral pneumonia is a specific type of viral pneumonia caused by adenovirus. 21. Pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae is a bacterial lung infection caused by this specific pathogen. 22. Pneumonia due to Haemophilus influenzae is a bacterial infection of the lungs caused by this organism. 23. Bacterial pneumonia, not elsewhere classified, includes infections caused by various bacteria, such as Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas, or Escherichia coli. 24. Pneumonia due to Klebsiella pneumoniae is a severe bacterial lung infection often associated with hospital settings. 25. Pneumonia due to Pseudomonas is a bacterial lung infection caused by Pseudomonas species, often seen in immunocompromised patients. 26. Pneumonia due to staphylococcus is caused by Staphylococcus bacteria, which can lead to abscess formation in the lungs. 27. Pneumonia due to group B streptococcus is a bacterial infection often seen in neonates. 28. Pneumonia due to other streptococci includes infections caused by non-group B Streptococcus species. 29. Pneumonia due to Escherichia coli is a bacterial lung infection caused by this enteric pathogen. 30. Pneumonia due to other aerobic Gram-negative bacteria includes infections caused by organisms such as Acinetobacter. 31. Pneumonia due to Mycoplasma pneumoniae is an atypical bacterial infection of the lungs. 32. Other bacterial pneumonia includes infections caused by less common bacterial pathogens. 33. Bacterial pneumonia, unspecified, refers to cases where the causative bacterial agent is not identified. 34. Pneumonia due to other infectious organisms includes infections caused by Chlamydia or other specified pathogens. 35. Chlamydial pneumonia is a lung infection caused by Chlamydia species. 36. Pneumonia in diseases classified elsewhere refers to lung infections secondary to other systemic diseases, such as bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic infections. 37. Bronchopneumonia, unspecified, is a type of pneumonia affecting the bronchi and surrounding lung tissue without a specified causative agent. 38. Lobar pneumonia, unspecified, involves infection of a single lobe of the lung without a specified causative agent. 39. Hypostatic pneumonia, unspecified, occurs due to prolonged immobility and pooling of secretions in the lungs. 40. Other pneumonia, organism unspecified, includes cases where the causative organism is not identified. 41. Pneumonia, unspecified, refers to cases where neither the causative organism nor the specific type of pneumonia is identified. 42. Acute bronchitis is an inflammation of the bronchi, typically caused by viral infections. 43. Acute bronchiolitis is an inflammation of the bronchioles, often seen in infants and young children. 44. Unspecified acute lower respiratory infection refers to infections of the lower respiratory tract without a specific diagnosis. 45. Vasomotor rhinitis is a non-allergic condition characterized by nasal congestion and rhinorrhea. 46. Allergic rhinitis due to pollen, also known as hay fever or pollinosis, is an allergic reaction to pollen. 47. Other seasonal allergic rhinitis refers to allergic reactions to seasonal allergens other than pollen. 48. Perennial allergic rhinitis is a year-round allergic condition caused by non-seasonal allergens. 49. Chronic rhinitis is a long-term inflammation of the nasal mucosa, which may include ozena, a condition characterized by atrophic rhinitis with foul-smelling crusts. 50. Chronic nasopharyngitis is a persistent inflammation of the nasopharynx. 51. Chronic pharyngitis is a long-term inflammation of the pharynx. 52. Chronic sinusitis is a prolonged inflammation of the sinuses, often associated with bacterial or fungal infections. 53. Nasal polyps are benign growths in the nasal cavity or sinuses. 54. Disorders of the nose and nasal sinuses include abscesses, cysts, deviated nasal septum, hypertrophy of nasal turbinates, and other specified conditions such as rhinoliths or perforation of the nasal septum.
